newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL strikers to go back to work Sunday.
newsitem.headline: PAL strikers to go back to work Sunday.

text.p: Striking ground staff of Philippine Airlines (PAL) ended a three-day strike on Saturday after the company agreed to finalise a new wage package by November 21, the airline said.

Only 120 out of the 243 scheduled international and domestic flights were flown during the strike by around 3,000 ground crew, most of them in flight registration and baggage and cargo handling services.
Flight schedules are expected to return to normal by Sunday noon, PAL officials said.

"We are victorious ... We have signed a memorandum of agreement where the minimum demands of the union were met," the national secretary of the PAL employees association (PALEA), Jose Penas III, told Reuters.
He said PAL management has agreed to stop hiring contractual workers as well as submit a counter-proposal to PALEA's 3.2 billion peso ($121 million) proposed package on November 5.

Included in the two-year wage package proposed by the workers were a 5,000 peso ($190) across-the-board increase, a 44 percent hike in average pay, a Christmas bonus of 150 percent of basic pay, a midyear bonus equivalent to one month's salary and an increase in overtime premium rates from 35.3 to 50 percent.
"A new collective bargaining agreement will be concluded by the two parties within 10 days from November 11, 1996," PAL said.
The two sides have been negotiating for a new salary package for over a year.
PALEA members went on strike on Wednesday after President Fidel Ramos refused to mediate in the dispute.
It was the third strike to hit the cash-strapped national air carrier in two years. ($1=26.285 pesos)
